After it, both carry EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_DRIFT at severity error, because runtime_config_check compares each deployment's declared live_strategies_contains against the runtime allowlist and a non-empty allowlist that omits their tags reads as a config change.

Nothing about those two books changed. They were stood down before and they are stood down now; no parameter, tag, twin pairing or book_params moved. But the recorded consequence is that both experiments' gate evaluation is blocked on an unresolved integrity event, so neither can be judged until someone classifies a drift that does not describe a real change.

The asymmetry looks unintended: standing every book down (empty allowlist) is modelled as a deliberate operational state, but standing all-but-one down is modelled as configuration drift. Running one canary at a time is the normal, desired shape - the risk envelope for WS-007 explicitly assumes 'LIVE_STRATEGIES names this canary alone while it runs' - so this will recur on every future canary.
